il_ferne_clyffe_state_park.blurb: Ferne Clyffe is a state park in southern Illinois, close to the town of Goreville, where sandstone cliffs stand in a canyon setting. Sport climbing is the focus, with a good number of top-rope routes, a few boulder problems and a small amount of trad. Grades cluster from 5.10 to 5.12, with a modest group of moderates at 5.9 and below and a few routes at 5.13 and 5.14. Many of the lines are steep or overhanging. Rebman Wall holds the most climbs of any sub-area, followed by The Ferne Clyffe Wall and Goreville Theatre.

il_mississippi_palisades.blurb: Mississippi Palisades is a state park on the Illinois bank of the Mississippi River, across from Iowa, with its climbing at the south end of the park near Savannah. The bluffs rise high above the river. Grades run from easy fifth class up to 5.12, with most routes between 5.6 and 5.10. Cooler, drier autumn weather is the favoured time to visit, while summers are humid and buggy. Sentinel holds the most climbs, followed by Twin Sisters and Bee Wall.

ma_weetamoo_area.blurb: Weetamoo is a bouldering zone inside Lynn Woods, on Massachusetts' North Shore north of Boston. Every climb here is a boulder problem, spanning V0 to V8, with the biggest group at V3 and a healthy spread of easier problems below it. The problems include slabs, arêtes and slopers. Reaching the boulders means a walk of roughly 25 to 30 minutes, first along a wide dirt road past a pond and then on a faint trail through the woods. The Tombstone Crag, Weetamoo Boulder and Summit Crag hold the most climbs.

nm_rabbit_ears_area.blurb: Rabbit Ears sits in the northern, granite part of the Organ Mountains, east of Las Cruces. Two parallel lines of peaks face each other across Rabbit Ears Canyon, a boulder-strewn drainage where the approach involves boulder-hopping, slabs and short scrambles. This is overwhelmingly a trad area, with multi-pitch routes common, a few sport and top-rope lines, and grades mostly from 5.6 to 5.10 plus a handful of 5.11s. Southern Comfort Wall is a sunny winter crag and The Citadel is a shady option for summer. The Citadel holds the most climbs, with North Rabbit Ear and Rabbit Ears Slabs next.

ut_vernal_area.blurb: Vernal is a desert climbing area in northeast Utah, with sandstone walls and towers set against the Uinta Mountains. The climbing is adventurous: the rock is soft or loose in places and older anchors are common. The mix is bouldering first, then trad, with a fair amount of sport and a few top-rope lines. Boulder problems mostly run V0 to V4, while roped routes cluster around 5.8 to 5.11, with 5.10 the most common. Dry Fork Canyon holds the most climbs and is mainly trad on sandstone, with some bouldering. Flag Crag and Moon Lake round out the larger sub-areas.
